title: Cycle 5 Explorer — rich
forward_vector: I am the manifest of Cycle 5 Explorer's rich face, its first round, a Study and still a proposal: one walk that builds the page's one idea from a strip of named notes and ends on a count of its claim, that each step darker lowers exactly one note (true with the tonic held, 90 of 90; with the notes held no note moves at all), and beside it the explorer itself, its own recorded voice, the rebuild's proofs beside the board, the steward's still that caught the grids clipping, and the review sheet that holds Loudon's four questions. I grow when the page is enriched again; I never hold the entry's words.

offers.what: 'Each step darker lowers exactly one note' is true with the tonic held and not with the notes held. Measured on the window piece's engine, which spells as the explorer does: holding the tonic, 90 of 90 darker steps (every tonic C♭ to C♯, six steps each) change exactly one note, each a half step down on the same letter, ♯4, 7, 3, 6, 2, 5 in that order. Holding the notes (the header's same notes, which the review sheet says the page opens on), 84 of 84 steps change no note at all: the tonic moves up a fifth and exactly one degree reads lower, the same six. Proposed: 'Each step darker with the tonic held lowers exactly one note: the one that falls off the window's sharp end comes back on its flat end, the same letter a half step lower. With the notes held, no note moves; home does.'

Two things the window shows that the section could say in a line, if Loudon wants them: turning the note ring one key flatward is the same move and also lowers exactly one note (98 of 98, mode held); and past Locrian the next note to leave would be the tonic itself (the window would become C♭ Lydian on C), which is why the walk from bright to dark has seven stops and not eight.

pieces.title: the rebuild on Paper · 2026-10-28 proof
pieces.caption: **The rebuild, beside the board above.** The page on its Paper ground at 1400 px, a headless screenshot from the day it was dressed. What the board couldn't do, done: every label on the ring stands upright, and the outside notes carry their own degrees and spellings (♯4 on F♯, ♭7 on B♭, the mode each is borrowed from). What it hasn't yet: the grids are bigger but already clip at this width (Scale Tones stops at 6, Chord Function cuts VII, Chord Tones drops its B column), the fault the class rehearsal measured below. The scroll calls this proof 'after a drag to E♭'; it shows C Ionian. The fonts are the fallback mono, since Google Fonts were not reachable from that run.

pieces.by: the Maker · Web Audio, the explorer's own voice and arithmetic
pieces.title: a seven-note window on the line of fifths · a walk in five steps
pieces.caption: **Does each step darker lower exactly one note?** Built up from nothing: the line of fifths alone, where seven places apart is the same letter a half step higher; a window of seven on it, every letter once; a tonic moved inside the window, where no note moves; the tonic held while the window slides, where one note falls off the sharp end and comes back seven places flat; and last the count, every darker step on every tonic from C♭ to C♯, both ways the explorer's header switch allows, then a short test of your ear. Checked headless against the piece's own engine and the explorer's own spelling: with the tonic held, 90 of 90 steps change exactly one note, each a half step down on the same letter, ♯4, 7, 3, 6, 2, 5 in order; with the notes held, 84 of 84 change no note, and the same one degree reads lower. Past Locrian the note to leave would be the tonic itself. What a listener hears was not checked.

pieces.title: the explorer itself · one file, Web Audio, Drafting Table
pieces.caption: **The page, playing.** Drag the note ring to change key and the degree ring to change mode; the T key switches what a mode change keeps. For modal interchange, press **Borrow one chord** under Guided moments, then the → key twice: the ♭VI stays borrowed in the new key. Silent until a click. It opens on C Ionian.
pieces.near: The hub is a small lit scope

pieces.title: the grids at 1440 px · the steward's class rehearsal, 2026-10-30
pieces.caption: **Bigger, but not yet whole.** I ♭VI IV V moved to D, the ♭VI still borrowed from Aeolian. The steward measured the grids at four widths: at 1280, 1440 and 1920 px Scale Tones and Chord Tones scroll sideways and hide their seventh column, and Chord Function hides its VII column from 1024 to 1440. Here the Scale Tones grid stops at 6. Found and measured, not yet fixed; the page waits on Loudon's review.

pieces.title: the page's own voice · 21.7 s, rendered offline
pieces.caption: **The explorer's sound, as its own code makes it**: the C major scale, the Diatonic cycle 5 preset at 88 bpm (Imaj7 IVmaj7 VII–7(♭5) III–7 VI–7 II–7 V7 Imaj7), then IV to minor IV. Rendered by the steward on 2026-10-30 with the page's audio routed to an offline renderer; every scale note within about 1 cent of its target, peak −6.5 dBFS, nothing clipped. Measured, not listened to.
pieces.near: stored as functions, so turning the key ring transposes them

pieces.title: the review sheet · the four questions on one page
pieces.caption: **The four questions, with what each needs to be answered.** Read out of the explorer's own code by the steward on 2026-10-30, printable, with tick boxes: every chord of the seven modes on C in all four dialects, the feel word per mode, and the roadmap to pick from. It notes that the page opens on same notes today, and that the tension chips run in fifths order.
